title: Vendor @object-ui/console as @objectstack/console, version-locked to framework releases
body:
## Summary

Vendor a pinned, prebuilt copy of `@object-ui/console` into the framework
release as a dedicated `@objectstack/console-dist` package, so a single
`pnpm add @objectstack/framework` always gives the user a version-matched
Console SPA — and Console releases no longer need to round-trip through
npm publish + a framework bump.

## Background

Today the runtime Console is consumed as a normal npm dependency:

- `package.json` → `"@object-ui/console": "^6.2.2"`
- `packages/cli/package.json` → same
- `packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts` resolves it at runtime via
  `require.resolve('@object-ui/console')` and mounts `dist/` at
  `/_console`. **There are zero `import` statements against the
  package** — it is purely a static-asset dependency.
- A sibling-repo dev fallback (`../objectui/apps/console`) already exists,
  which acknowledges the real coupling.

Meanwhile in `objectstack-ai/cloud` we deliberately bypass npm for
this exact dependency:

- `.objectui-sha` pins a commit
- The Dockerfile checks out objectui as a sibling, builds
  `@object-ui/console` (and `@object-ui/studio` for objectos), and
  `cp -r`s the `dist/` over `node_modules/@object-ui/{console,studio}`
- `require.resolve` in framework's CLI picks up the overlay transparently

The framework story should mirror this for the same reason: the Console
SPA is **runtime-coupled to a specific framework version** (v6 console
must pair with v6 framework — see `apps/account/CHANGELOG.md` where
console + studio + framework are bumped together), so making the
end-user manage two npm versions adds friction without buying
flexibility.

> Note: `@object-ui/i18n` is a real JS import (39+ call sites in
> `apps/account`) and **must keep going through npm publish + framework
> bump**. This proposal only covers the static-asset Console SPA.

## Proposal

### 1. New package `packages/console-dist/`

A dist-only npm package whose sole role is shipping the prebuilt
Console SPA, version-locked to the framework release:

```
packages/console-dist/
├── package.json          # name: "@objectstack/console-dist"
├── README.md             # clearly states: "prebuilt @object-ui/console
│                         #  pinned to this framework version; for source
│                         #  see github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui"
└── dist/                 # built in CI, NOT committed
```

`package.json` skeleton:

```json
{
  "name": "@objectstack/console-dist",
  "version": "<tracks framework>",
  "description": "Prebuilt @object-ui/console SPA pinned to this framework release.",
  "files": ["dist", "README.md"],
  "exports": { "./package.json": "./package.json" },
  "license": "Apache-2.0"
}
```

### 2. Pin objectui by SHA, build in CI

Mirror the cloud repo's mechanics:

```
.objectui-sha                          # pinned commit, single source of truth
scripts/bump-objectui.sh               # bump helper (port from cloud)
scripts/build-console-dist.sh          # checkout sibling objectui@SHA,
                                       # pnpm install + build,
                                       # cp dist → packages/console-dist/dist/
```

`build-console-dist.sh` runs **before `pnpm publish`** in the release
workflow. The `dist/` directory is gitignored — it only exists in CI
publish artifacts and in local dev when you opt in.

### 3. Update `resolveConsolePath()`

In `packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts`, prefer the vendored copy and
keep `@object-ui/console` as fallback (so cloud's `cp -r` overlay and
manual user installs still win when present):

```ts
const CONSOLE_PACKAGES = [
  '@objectstack/console-dist',   // 1. framework-paired build (default)
  '@object-ui/console',          // 2. user/cloud overlay
];
```

This ordering needs verification against the cloud Docker overlay
flow — cloud overrides should still take precedence in cloud images.
One option: cloud's overlay script writes to **both** package locations,
or framework prefers `@object-ui/console` when its version > vendored
version. To discuss in the design review.

### 4. Demote the npm dep

Move `@object-ui/console` from `dependencies` → `devDependencies`
(used for local dev / type checking) in both root and `packages/cli`.
End users no longer install it directly.

## Naming

Recommended: **`@objectstack/console-dist`**.

The `-dist` suffix makes the role explicit ("this is a build artifact,
not a source package"), avoiding confusion with `@object-ui/console`
which remains the canonical, independently-released SPA from the
`objectstack-ai/objectui` repo. The two coexist with distinct roles:

| Package | Owner | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `@object-ui/console` | objectui repo | Standalone Console SPA, independent release channel, usable by cloud overlay or anyone who wants to consume it directly |
| `@objectstack/console-dist` | framework repo | Prebuilt SPA frozen at the SHA this framework release was tested against; ships as a framework runtime asset |

Alternatives considered: `@objectstack/console-assets`,
`@objectstack/runtime-console`, `@objectstack/console` (rejected —
too ambiguous vs `@object-ui/console`).

## Alternatives considered

### A. Vendor into `packages/cli/vendor/`

Rejected: bloats the CLI tarball, and conceptually CLI is just one
consumer (account app, future server adapters, edge runtime variants
would all need to reach into the CLI package to find the SPA — wrong
direction).

### B. A top-level `vendor/` directory

Rejected: doesn't ship via npm, so npm-installed users wouldn't get it
at all.

### C. Keep status quo, only add `.objectui-sha` for CI test pinning

Rejected: doesn't solve the underlying problem that Console releases
still need an npm publish + framework version bump round-trip.

### D. A virtual package `@objectstack/console` (no `-dist` suffix)

Considered. The naming collision with `@object-ui/console` creates
ecosystem confusion ("which one do I install?"). `-dist` suffix avoids
this.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `packages/console-dist/` exists with `package.json` + `README.md`
- [ ] `.objectui-sha` committed; `scripts/bump-objectui.sh` works
- [ ] `scripts/build-console-dist.sh` produces `packages/console-dist/dist/`
      from a sibling objectui checkout at the pinned SHA
- [ ] Release workflow runs `build-console-dist.sh` before `pnpm publish`
      and publishes `@objectstack/console-dist` at the same version as
      `@objectstack/framework`
- [ ] `resolveConsolePath()` resolves `@objectstack/console-dist` first,
      falls back to `@object-ui/console`
- [ ] `@object-ui/console` demoted to `devDependencies`
- [ ] A fresh `pnpm add @objectstack/framework` in an empty project mounts
      `/_console` without any extra install steps
- [ ] Cloud Docker overlay flow (`cp -r` over `@object-ui/console`)
      still wins in cloud images — verified by deploying a cloud build
      that overrides Console and confirming the overlay version is served
- [ ] `@object-ui/i18n` continues going through npm publish + framework
      bump (unchanged)

## Out of scope

- Studio SPA — currently only consumed by cloud's `objectos` image,
  not directly by framework runtime. If/when framework starts mounting
  `/_studio` natively, apply the same pattern with
  `@objectstack/studio-dist`.
- `@object-ui/i18n` — stays on npm publish, see note above.

## Related

- `objectstack-ai/cloud`: `.objectui-sha`, `scripts/bump-objectui.sh`,
  `apps/cloud/Dockerfile`, `apps/objectos/Dockerfile` —
  reference implementation of the SHA-pin + sibling-build pattern
- `objectstack-ai/objectui` — source of truth for `@object-ui/console`
